name: Night Rain Regalia (Dạ Vũ Tam Bảo)

bonuses.rule: while your rain field (The Night Is Long) stands or the umbrella is open, every hit you evade rings the chain; at three rings a bolt falls on the foe who struck at you, dealing Lightning damage scaled by your Metal. A holder whose root has no Thunder can still call this bolt; it is the only Thunder the Regalia gives.

story: The founder held all three, and so did Mạnh Dạ Vũ until 1166. When the halls moved to Thần Cổ Phong, the chain stayed on the eaves of the old tower over Tàn Hà Hồ, because nobody would take it down, and Quan Vũ Thanh keeps it there. The Regalia has not been whole since. The head says a chain is not a thing one carries. Mạnh Lưu Ly says a head who cannot take it down is not the founder's heir.

name: Lamp and Shears of the Vaults (Hồn Khố Song Bảo)

bonuses.rule: once a fight, a cursed foe below a quarter of their health has their curse turned into a seal: they cannot cast arts for 2 s.

story: By the vault law of 1010, a life lamp can be put out from afar only by the master lamp and the shears together, in two hands. Lệ Tiêu Hồn holds the lamp and gave the shears to his niece Ninh Tịch Đăng, so that he could never do it alone. She has refused him once.

name: Keeper of the Old Tower (Cựu Lâu Thủ)

bonuses.rule: for the first 5 s of each fight you take 25 % less damage while you cast no damaging art; each hit you evade in that time stores one Water buff stack, and your first sword art after it spends them all for 8 % more damage each.

story: The sword and the half-tally are both from 803, the year of the truce, and Quan has carried them together since the founder died. She wears them beside the founder's rain-chain, which belongs to the Night Rain Regalia, not to her. The pair is whole on her; the Regalia is not.

name: Keeper of Kinh Lôi Mạch (Kinh Lôi Mạch Thủ)

bonuses.rule: a foe carrying two or more of your curses is branded. Each of your Lightning bolts that lands on a branded foe adds 1 s to every curse it carries (the curse duration clamp still holds).

story: Cast together in 1170, when Lệ moved the vaults into the vein. The master lamp is not part of it: by the vault law of 1010 the lamp is half of a pair kept in two hands, and it stays burning in the vaults while he goes out with the brand, the bell and the Ninth Tribulation seal. He made this pair so as to have something whole of his own.

name: The Undefeated (Bất Bại Song Kiện)

bonuses.rule: each second you go without attacking adds 12 % crit damage to your next sword art. The first sword art of each fight cannot be evaded. Return to the Scabbard (Quy Sao): after 3 s in which you fire no damaging art, the foe counts as unstruck again: No Second Cut and the first-art clause re-arm.

story: Both come from Kinh Điện: the sword her father forged in 656 and the mail the Tower forged her in 1166 from the same mine. She wears them with the catalogue's Unbroken Edge ring, which keeps her drawn-out cut whole between strikes. Phượng Minh's right wing fan hangs in her room as a trophy and is not part of it.

name: Glass Storm (Lưu Ly Phong Lôi)

bonuses.rule: while you are above half health, each Lightning crit chains one more bolt. Each time a single hit takes more than a tenth of your health, your next Lightning art fires at once. Healing on you is 20 % weaker, because the glass does not mend.

story: Made around her by the two people who raised her: the forge master's glass sword, Quan's robe and the rod she cut herself. She keeps all three, and the Tower watches what she does with them.

name: Ears of the Hall (Hồi Âm Tam Bảo)

bonuses.rule: you always evade the first art a foe casts at you each fight, and the bell rings a ward on you worth 8 % of your health. A foe you have heard is marked, and your seals on a marked foe last 2 s longer.

story: The bell Ân Thanh Linh cast in 1030, the mirror of the Hall's founder and the robe of the trade. All three belong to the Hall of Echoes, not to the Tower, and pass with the Hall from mother to daughter.

name: Drum of the Gate (Lôi Môn Cổ Bảo)

bonuses.rule: every fourth storm stack you lay beats the drum. The raised sword draws one bolt onto the foe, and the foe gains 2 Slowed Time stacks. Each beat in the same fight adds one more Slowed Time stack.

story: Stick, drum and sword are all of one peach tree on Tử Tinh, if the Hầu family is right. Hầu Vọng Xuân holds all three. He says the Xuân Lôi Cổ would make it four, and his master hears him say it.

name: Gold Sand and Lightning (Sa Kim Lôi)

bonuses.rule: while your sword is raised to the cloud, each bolt it draws that crits adds a Lightning stack on the foe.

story: Both come from Sa Kim Khoáng: her mother's leather and her father's ore. She wears both, and she does not ask how the forge was paid.

name: Hearing the Spring Rain (Thính Xuân Vũ)

bonuses.rule: the first hit the foe aims at you is heard. If you evade it, your next sword art at the foe is a sure crit.

story: The head gave him both in 1186, the year he took him, the first gift he had made a disciple in a century. The Tower reads more into it than the boy does.

name: Thunder on the Cone (Sơn Hỏa Lôi)

bonuses.rule: each Fire hit you land counts as half a Lightning hit for your Thunder arts' stacks and chains.

story: One piece from the outer gate and one from the old tower. At Luyện Khí she can wear only the sword; the ring waits in her box for the day she reaches Trúc Cơ, by the inner gate's rule or against it.
